claim.why_it_matters: The ACCEPT GR 13 table of screen-item categories and their figurative constants is one table in the PDF. The transcription splits it in two: the Alphanumeric-edited row falls out as loose text, and the second table makes 'Boolean | ZEROS' its header row. A reader or tool that parses the tables loses the Alphanumeric-edited mapping and treats Boolean as a column heading.

verdict.reasoning: Printed page 434 (folio 412) at 300 dpi shows ONE two-column table under the heading 'Screen item / Figurative constant' with eight rows in order: Alphabetic, Alphanumeric, Alphanumeric-edited (all Alphanumeric SPACES), Boolean ZEROS, National and National-edited (National SPACES), Numeric and Numeric-edited (ZEROS). page-434.md lines 3-15 hold a first table (header + Alphabetic, Alphanumeric), then the line '   Alphanumeric-edited Alphanumeric SPACES' as a loose paragraph outside any table, then a second table whose HEADER row is '| Boolean | ZEROS |' followed by the separator and the remaining four rows. No words are lost, so a human reading in order still recovers every mapping, but the table structure is genuinely corrupted: the Alphanumeric-edited row is no longer a table row and the Boolean row is demoted to a column heading. Any mechanical table parse loses the Alphanumeric-edited -> Alphanumeric SPACES mapping and misreads Boolean/ZEROS as headers. This is more than wrapping or furniture; the claim quotes both sources accurately and its 'structural' severity (not normative) is right.
